records.text: The board gave the proposal short shrift, and the CFO was left to carry the can.

artifact.comprehensible: The board did not spend much time on the proposal and did not think it was important. Because of this, the CFO had to take the blame alone.

glosses.gloss: did not give the proposal much attention or time; treated it quickly and without care
glosses.example: The teacher gave my question short shrift and moved on to the next topic.

glosses.gloss: to be the person who takes the blame or responsibility for something bad, even if others were also involved
glosses.example: When the project failed, the manager had to carry the can for the whole team.

artifact.translation: 董事会没有重视这个提案，结果首席财务官不得不独自承担责任。

records.text: He bottled it at the last minute and threw his colleagues under the bus.

artifact.comprehensible: At the last minute, he lost his courage and did something that hurt his colleagues instead of taking the blame himself.

glosses.gloss: lost your courage and failed to do something you were supposed to do
glosses.example: He was going to ask her to marry him, but he bottled it and said nothing.

glosses.expression: threw his colleagues under the bus
glosses.gloss: did something that hurt your friends or co-workers in order to save yourself
glosses.example: When the boss asked who made the mistake, she threw her team under the bus and said it was their fault.

artifact.translation: 他在最后一刻退缩了，还为了自保而坑了同事。

records.text: Not until the auditors had gone did the manager admit that the figures had been doctored.

artifact.comprehensible: The manager did not admit that someone had changed the figures to trick people until after the auditors had left.

glosses.gloss: changed in a dishonest way to trick people
glosses.example: He doctored the photo to make it look like he was on a beach.

glosses.gloss: people whose job is to check financial records
glosses.example: The auditors looked at all the company's bank records.

artifact.grammar: The sentence starts with 'Not until...', which moves the negative idea to the front. This makes the main clause use question-like word order: 'did the manager admit' instead of 'the manager admitted'. The meaning is: the manager admitted only after the auditors had gone.
artifact.translation: 直到审计员离开之后，经理才承认那些数字被人篡改过。

records.text: The house stood in a state of genteel decay, its occupants having long since repaired to the Continent.

artifact.comprehensible: The house was in a state of polite and quiet decay. The people who lived there had moved to the Continent a long time ago.

glosses.gloss: a kind of slow falling apart that still looks polite and a little grand, not rough or dirty
glosses.example: The old hotel had a genteel decay: the paint was coming off, but the chairs were still soft and the tea was still good.

glosses.gloss: went to, especially in a formal or old-fashioned way
glosses.example: After the long dinner, the guests repaired to the garden to talk.

glosses.gloss: the main part of Europe, not including Britain
glosses.example: Every summer, my aunt leaves London and goes to the Continent for a month.

artifact.grammar: The phrase 'its occupants having long since repaired to the Continent' is a participle clause. It gives the reason or background for the house's state. It does not have a helping verb like 'had'. You can understand it as 'because its occupants had moved to the Continent a long time before'.
artifact.translation: 这座房子处于一种体面而缓慢的衰败状态，因为它的住户早已移居欧洲大陆。

records.text: The findings are suggestive rather than conclusive, and ought not to be over-read.

artifact.comprehensible: The results hint at something, but they do not prove it. People should not read too much into them.

glosses.gloss: hinting at something but not proving it
glosses.example: His smile was suggestive rather than conclusive; it might mean he liked the plan, but he did not say yes.

glosses.gloss: to understand or interpret something as having more meaning or importance than it really has
glosses.example: Do not over-read her short message; she was just busy, not angry.

artifact.grammar: The phrase 'ought not to be over-read' is passive: it means 'people should not over-read them'. The subject 'The findings' is the thing that should not be over-read, not the person doing the reading.
artifact.translation: 这些发现只是提示性的，并非定论，因此不应过度解读。

records.text: The lessee shall indemnify the lessor against all claims arising from any breach of the covenants herein.

artifact.comprehensible: The person who rents the thing must protect the owner from any claims that come from breaking any of the promises in this agreement.

glosses.gloss: to protect someone from loss or damage by paying for it
glosses.example: The insurance company will indemnify you if your car is stolen.

glosses.gloss: the person who pays to use something for a time
glosses.example: The lessee must pay rent every month.

glosses.gloss: the person who owns something and lets someone else use it for pay
glosses.example: The lessor can end the agreement if the rent is late.

glosses.gloss: formal promises in a legal agreement
glosses.example: The contract has many covenants that both sides must follow.

glosses.gloss: a breaking of a law or agreement
glosses.example: Not paying the rent is a breach of the contract.

glosses.gloss: demands for money or rights
glosses.example: The company received many claims after the accident.

glosses.gloss: in this document
glosses.example: The rules herein apply to all workers.

artifact.grammar: The sentence uses legal language and passive-like structure. 'The lessee shall indemnify the lessor against all claims' means the lessee must protect the lessor from claims. 'Arising from any breach of the covenants herein' tells you what kind of claims: those that come from breaking the promises in this agreement.
artifact.translation: 承租人应赔偿出租人因违反本协议中的承诺而引起的所有索赔。

records.text: The report stops short of apportioning blame, but the implications are hard to miss.

artifact.comprehensible: The report does not go as far as saying who is to blame. But it is very easy to see what it suggests.

glosses.gloss: does not go as far as; does not do something completely
glosses.example: She stopped short of calling him a liar, but everyone understood what she meant.

glosses.gloss: saying who is responsible for something bad
glosses.example: The teacher did not apportion blame for the broken window; she just asked what happened.

glosses.gloss: very easy to notice or understand
glosses.example: The sign was huge, so it was hard to miss.

artifact.translation: 报告没有走到指责谁的地步，但其中暗示的意思很难不被注意到。

records.text: He was, to put it mildly, not best pleased with the outcome.

artifact.comprehensible: He was very unhappy with what happened. To say it in a gentle way, he was not at all pleased.

glosses.gloss: used to say that you are describing something in a gentle or soft way, when the real situation is stronger
glosses.example: The food was bad, to put it mildly; I couldn't eat it.

glosses.gloss: very unhappy or annoyed
glosses.example: She was not best pleased when she saw the broken window.

artifact.translation: 说得客气一点，他对这个结果很不高兴。

records.text: What the committee had taken for a routine oversight was in fact a deliberate omission, designed to spare the minister an awkward question.

artifact.comprehensible: The committee thought it was just a normal mistake. But it was not a mistake. Someone left it out on purpose. They did this so the minister would not have to answer a difficult question.

glosses.gloss: thought to be; believed to be
glosses.example: I took the tall man for a teacher, but he was a student.

glosses.gloss: a normal mistake made because someone forgot to do something
glosses.example: Forgetting to sign the form was a routine oversight, not a big problem.

glosses.gloss: leaving something out on purpose
glosses.example: Her name was missing from the list. It was a deliberate omission, not an accident.

glosses.gloss: save someone from something difficult or unpleasant
glosses.example: He told a small lie to spare her feelings.

glosses.gloss: a difficult question that is embarrassing to answer
glosses.example: The reporter asked an awkward question about the money.

artifact.grammar: The sentence has a contrast: 'What the committee had taken for a routine oversight' is the subject, and 'was in fact a deliberate omission' is the main verb. The phrase 'designed to spare...' describes the omission. The structure is not too hard, but the long subject at the start may confuse. Break it down: [The thing that the committee thought was a mistake] was really [a deliberate omission].
artifact.translation: 委员会原以为那只是一次普通的疏忽，但实际上那是故意省略的，目的是让部长不必回答一个尴尬的问题。

records.text: The company was on the hook for a sum it could ill afford.

artifact.comprehensible: The company had to pay an amount of money that it could not really pay.

glosses.gloss: responsible for paying money or for something bad
glosses.example: My brother lost his phone, and now I am on the hook for a new one.

glosses.gloss: not able to pay for something without difficulty; can hardly afford
glosses.example: She lives on a small pension and can ill afford a big doctor's bill.

artifact.grammar: The phrase 'a sum it could ill afford' means 'a sum that it could ill afford'. The word 'that' is left out, so the clause 'it could ill afford' directly follows 'a sum' and describes it. This is common in English but can be hard to follow.
artifact.translation: 这家公司必须支付一笔它几乎负担不起的款项。

records.text: The reaction proceeds only in the presence of a catalyst, without which the activation energy is prohibitively high.

artifact.comprehensible: The reaction happens only when a catalyst is there. If there is no catalyst, the activation energy is too high, so the reaction cannot happen.

glosses.gloss: happens or goes forward
glosses.example: The meeting proceeds even if the manager is late.

glosses.gloss: when something is there
glosses.example: Plants grow well in the presence of sunlight.

glosses.gloss: a substance that makes a chemical reaction go faster without being used up
glosses.example: A catalyst helps the reaction go faster.

glosses.gloss: if it is not there
glosses.example: I need my glasses, without which I cannot read.

glosses.gloss: the energy needed to start a chemical reaction
glosses.example: The activation energy for this reaction is very high.

glosses.gloss: so high that it stops something from happening
glosses.example: The cost of the car was prohibitively high, so we did not buy it.

artifact.grammar: The phrase 'without which' introduces a condition: it means 'if there is no catalyst'. The main clause says the reaction happens only with a catalyst; the 'without which' clause explains what happens without it.
artifact.translation: 该反应只有在催化剂存在时才能进行；没有催化剂，活化能高得使反应无法发生。

records.text: It behoves us to consider whether such a course of action is consonant with our obligations.

artifact.comprehensible: We should think about whether doing something like this agrees with what we must do.

glosses.gloss: it is right or necessary for us
glosses.example: It behoves us to help a friend who is in trouble.

glosses.gloss: a way of doing something; a plan
glosses.example: The teacher chose a course of action to help the class learn faster.

glosses.gloss: in agreement with; matching
glosses.example: His words are consonant with his actions.

glosses.gloss: the things we must do because of duty or rules
glosses.example: We must meet our obligations and pay the money back on time.

artifact.grammar: The sentence uses 'whether' to introduce a clause that is the object of 'consider'. The subject is 'it', which stands for the idea of considering. The phrase 'such a course of action' refers to a way of acting like the one just mentioned. The structure is formal but not inverted.
artifact.translation: 我们应该考虑这样的做法是否符合我们的义务。
